name: Virginia
nameStory: Virginia is named for the fact that Queen Elizabeth I never married. She was called the Virgin Queen, and Walter Raleigh flattered her by naming the whole claim after it. An entire state is named after a monarch's marital status.
capitalStory: William Byrd II stood on a hill above the James River, decided the bend looked just like the view at Richmond upon Thames back in London, and used the name. That hill later became the Confederate capital - only about 100 miles from Washington, DC.

majorFeatures.note: Jamestown, Richmond, and the road inland

funFacts: Eight presidents were born in Virginia, more than any other state - hence 'Mother of Presidents.'
Jamestown, founded 1607, was the first permanent English settlement in North America.
Virginia is officially a Commonwealth, not a state.
The Shenandoah Valley runs southwest to northeast, which made it a perfect invasion route in both directions during the Civil War.
whyItMatters: Washington and Richmond, the two wartime capitals, sat about 100 miles apart. That short stretch of Virginia became the bloodiest ground in American history, and the war finally ended at Appomattox Court House, also in Virginia.
